issues.description: Field StockIngredient.price: the template repository declares the field as type double, while the problem statement UML and the solution repository declare it as type int. This inconsistency means students looking at the template will use a double for price but the specification and reference solution expect an int, leading to confusion about the intended numeric type and potential mismatches when implementing or comparing code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's StockIngredient.price declaration from double to int so it matches the UML and the solution. Adjust any internal usage in the template (constructor, getter, and any arithmetic) to use int consistently.

issues.description: Method StockIngredient.getPrice(): the template declares getPrice() to return double, whereas the problem statement UML and the solution repository use int for the ingredient price and have getPrice() returning int. This return-type mismatch confuses students about the expected type when summing prices (e.g., calculateTotalPrice) and can cause type inconsistencies when following the UML or the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's getPrice() signature and return type to int (public int getPrice()) and ensure the backing field is an int, matching the UML and the solution. Update any code that consumes getPrice() if necessary to expect int.

issues.description: Constructor StockIngredient(String, price, int): the template constructor signature accepts (String name, double price, int quantity), but the UML and the solution expect (String name, int price, int quantity). This parameter type mismatch for the price argument will confuse students following the UML and can cause compilation/type errors when they try to instantiate StockIngredient according to the specification or compare against the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template constructor signature to public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) and update its parameter validation and assignments to use int for price, aligning the constructor parameters with the UML and the solution.
